notes: Fix: the single BATT port was used twice, by the battery + and - leads. The MKR Zero's JST battery connector is now two ports, BATT.+ and BATT.-, so each is used once. The battery + goes to BATT.+ and the battery - goes to BATT.-.
The parts are unchanged from step 1.

The DHT22 sits in breadboard row a, columns 26 to 29, in pin order VCC, SDA (data), NC, GND. The exact holes are read from the image. The red, orange and black jumpers go in row b of the VCC, data and GND columns. The 100nF capacitor goes between columns 26 and 29 in row d. The 4.75k pull-up goes between columns 26 and 27 in row e.

The MKR Zero is not plugged into the breadboard in the image, even though the text says to plug it in. Three jumper wires connect it: VCC to DHT22 power (3.3V), GND to DHT22 ground, and D7 to DHT22 data.
The image is taken as authority. The short blue and yellow strokes are treated as component leads, not extra wires.

The microSD card goes in the MKR Zero slot, modelled as the SD port. The MKR Zero is a new part type because lookup_part did not find it. The 100nF capacitor uses the non-polarised capacitor-22pf type with value=100nF.
